page_hint: Chapter 3 §1, §2, §3, §6, §8; Tables 3-2 and 3-3; boxed rule; Qwen transfer; mini-case
quoted_clause: A 70B dense model reads all 70B weights (or close to it) for every token
observed: The chapter repeatedly treats weight-read traffic as a per-token quantity: 'reads all 70B weights ... for every token'; 'FP16 active weight-read per token ~25.6 GB'; 'active weight-read traffic (~25.6 GB of weights read per token)'; '~12 GB read per token'; '~25.6 GB of active weight footprint is read per token'; Table 3-3 'FP16 weight-read per token'.
correction: Introduce a third accounting line: 'weight-read per forward pass' or 'weight-read per batch step'. State explicitly that the 140 GB / 25.6 GB figures are batch=1 single-token decode values; for prefill or batch size B, weight traffic is amortized and, for MoE, depends on the union of routed experts. Replace 'read per token' with 'read per forward pass (batch=1 decode)' or 'per-token amortized at batch size B' wherever the claim is not scoped to batch=1.
acceptance_test: Every occurrence of 'weight-read per token' is either explicitly scoped to batch=1 single-token decode or replaced by per-forward-pass/per-batch-step language. No sentence claims a dense 70B model reads 140 GB of weights for every token in a batched or prefill forward pass.
verdict_evidence: ch3:11, 72, 99, 176, 195 state 'weight-read per token' unscoped (grep 'batch|amortiz' in ch3 returns nothing), while ch2:97 scopes the same 140 GB as 'batch-1-equivalent ... before batching/amortization'.
fix_instruction: Scope each 'weight-read per token' figure to batch-1 decode, or use per-forward-pass/per-batch-step wording with the amortization caveat.

page_hint: Chapter 3 §7, 'What We Still Don't Know', first bullet
quoted_clause: the actual fraction of active parameters may vary with prompt content, token position, and expert availability
observed: The text says the active-parameter fraction per token may vary with prompt content, token position, and expert availability.
correction: Rewrite the bullet to say: 'Which experts are active varies with prompt content and token position; the number of active parameters per token is fixed by top-k and expert size under standard routing. Effective active count can vary only under variable-k, capacity dropping, or expert-unavailable fallback, which should be stated as an implementation-specific exception.'
acceptance_test: The text no longer claims that the active-parameter fraction varies with prompt content under fixed top-k routing; any variability claim is explicitly tied to variable-k, capacity dropping, or expert unavailability.
verdict_evidence: ch3:164 says the 'fraction of active parameters may vary with prompt content, token position'. Under fixed top-k with equal-size experts (ch3:70: top-2 of 8 = 12.8B) the active count per token is fixed; only which experts are active varies (ch27:30).
fix_instruction: Say which experts are active varies; active count is fixed by top-k and expert size, except under variable-k, capacity dropping, or expert fallback.

quoted_clause: where that shape is not known, as if the model were dense (the conservative bound)
observed: The key takeaway says that when attention shape is unknown, provision KV as if the model were dense, calling that the conservative bound.
correction: Replace 'as if the model were dense' with 'as if the model used full multi-head attention at the same layer count and hidden width' or 'at the dense full-MHA rate'. Keep 'dense' for parameter allocation only.
acceptance_test: The key takeaway and any parallel wording distinguish parameter allocation (dense/MoE) from attention shape (full-MHA/GQA/MQA) and identify full-MHA, not dense, as the conservative KV bound.
verdict_evidence: ch3:95 makes 'as if the model were dense' the conservative KV bound, but ch3:91 shows a dense model with the challenger's 32L/4096H GQA shape holds the same ~0.60 GB, and ch3:176 says 'dense full-MHA rate'.
fix_instruction: Replace 'as if the model were dense' with 'at the full-MHA rate for the same layer count and hidden width'.

observed: Tables 3-1, 3-2, and 3-3 label the FLOP figure 'per forward pass' while the derivation is 70B × 2 FLOP/param and 12.8B × 2 FLOP/param, which is per token, not per forward pass over the 9.2K-token input.
correction: Change the metric label to 'FLOPs per token (batch=1 decode)' or 'FLOPs per token forward pass'. If a per-sequence figure is intended, multiply by the token count and label it 'FLOPs per 9.2K-token prefill'.
acceptance_test: Every FLOP table row states whether the value is per token or per sequence, and the derivation matches the label.
verdict_evidence: ch3:57/73/197 label 70B x 2 FLOP/param = ~0.14T as 'per forward pass', but that is per token; the 9.2K-context forward pass is 1.29 PFLOP (ch2:102), and ch3:81 writes FLOP_MoE/token for the same quantity.
fix_instruction: Relabel the rows 'FLOPs per token (batch-1 decode forward pass)', or give the per-9.2K-sequence figure.

quoted_clause: Routing still emits one key and one value per token per layer
observed: The text attributes K/V emission to routing: 'Routing still emits one key and one value per token per layer'.
correction: Replace with: 'The attention layers still emit one key and one value per token per layer; routing in the feed-forward sub-layer neither reduces nor increases that count.'
acceptance_test: The text no longer says routing emits K/V; K/V emission is attributed to attention layers.
verdict_evidence: ch3:91 'Routing still emits one key and one value per token per layer' mis-attributes K/V emission; the same sentence's tail and the mini-case (ch3:176) correctly attribute it to the attention layers.
fix_instruction: Change the subject to 'The attention layers still emit one key and one value per token per layer; routing neither reduces nor increases that count.'

page_hint: Chapter 3 §6, 'One verified 2026 transfer: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next', KV cache bullet
quoted_clause: QSA attends sparsely at micro-block granularity — so per-token KV no longer follows the dense formula
observed: The text says Qwen's hybrid attention attacks the KV constant at the mechanism level because GDN keeps a fixed-size recurrent state and QSA attends sparsely, and concludes that per-token KV no longer follows the dense formula.
correction: Separate the two mechanisms: 'GDN layers keep a fixed-size recurrent state, so their per-token KV does not grow linearly. QSA layers sparsify attention reads; whether they also reduce stored KV depends on the cache implementation. If QSA stores full K/V, those layers still follow the dense per-token KV formula.' Cite the QSA cache mechanism or remove the claim that QSA changes the KV constant.
acceptance_test: The text states explicitly whether QSA changes KV residency or only attention compute; it does not infer reduced KV storage from sparse attention alone.
verdict_evidence: ch3:144 infers reduced KV residency from QSA's micro-block sparsity. The book's own Ch 7 prices the saving via GDN fixed state plus the 16-full-attention/48-GDN split (ch7:114-116) and lists Flash-Next as 'mechanism claim, no stated KV metric' (ch7:266).
fix_instruction: Attribute the KV change to GDN state and the attention-layer fraction; say QSA sparsity cuts attention reads, not stored KV; note no stated KV metric.

page_hint: Chapter 3 §8, mini-case, second paragraph and final paragraph
quoted_clause: we provision at the dense-model rate (~12 GB at 8-bit, ~24 GB at FP16) either way as the conservative bound
observed: The mini-case first says 'where the shape is not known we provision at the dense full-MHA rate', then later says 'we provision at the dense-model rate ... either way as the conservative bound' even after stating the challenger's known 32L/4096H GQA shape.
correction: Rewrite: 'When the attention shape is unknown, provision at the dense full-MHA rate as the conservative bound. When the shape is known—as it is for the challenger—use the model's own shape. Routing does not change the bytes either way.'
acceptance_test: The mini-case no longer says to use the dense rate when the shape is known; the condition for the conservative bound is explicitly 'shape unknown'.
verdict_evidence: ch3:176 conditions the dense full-MHA rate on 'where the shape is not known', but ch3:178 says 'we provision at the dense-model rate (~12 GB at 8-bit, ~24 GB at FP16) either way as the conservative bound' after stating the challenger's known GQA shape (0.6 GB).
fix_instruction: Scope the conservative bound to 'shape unknown'; when the shape is known use the model's own shape; label ~12 GB as the dense-70B full-MHA rate.

quoted_clause: in MoE pre-training, a routing loss directs each token to the most relevant expert(s), and the unused experts receive no gradient for that step
observed: The text describes MoE training as a 'routing loss' that directs each token to the most relevant experts and says unused experts receive no gradient for that step.
correction: Rewrite: 'In MoE pre-training, a learned gating network selects top-k experts per token; an auxiliary load-balancing loss is usually added to encourage expert use. Experts not selected for a given token receive no gradient from that token at that step.'
acceptance_test: The text no longer describes a 'routing loss' that directly directs tokens; it distinguishes learned gating from auxiliary load balancing.
verdict_evidence: ch3:16 'a routing loss directs each token to the most relevant expert(s)': learned gates/top-k select (ch3:12, ch27:30); an auxiliary load-balancing loss does not direct selection. 'Unused experts receive no gradient for that step' holds per token, not per step.
fix_instruction: Say a learned gate selects top-k experts per token, with an auxiliary load-balancing loss; unselected experts get no gradient from that token.

quoted_clause: The durable mental model: total parameters set the ceiling; active parameters per token set the floor.
observed: This compression is ambiguous and can mislead on memory: total parameters set a lower bound on weight residency (all weights must be resident unless offloaded), not a ceiling for memory; active parameters set a lower bound on per-token compute and active weight-read traffic, not a floor for residency.
correction: Reword as: 'total parameters bound the maximum active work and set the residency floor; active parameters per token set the compute floor (and active weight-read traffic).'
acceptance_test: A reader can state that total parameters drive weight residency and active parameters drive per-token compute without inferring that total is a memory ceiling.
verdict_evidence: ch3 §2: 'the full 140 GB is the residency floor' two sentences before 'total parameters set the ceiling; active parameters per token set the floor' — same quantity named floor then ceiling, and the budget (memory vs compute) is never named.
fix_instruction: Name the budget in each half: e.g. 'total parameters set the memory ceiling — and, in a dense model, the residency floor; active parameters per token set the compute floor'.
